q: Following the 1937 provincial elections, Congress ministries were formed in which of the following provinces (initially, and later)?
o: Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, United Provinces, Bihar, and later NWFP and Assam
Only in Muslim-majority provinces
Only Bengal, Punjab and Sindh
All eleven provinces uniformly from the start

q: Despite generally liberalising civil liberties, which of the following incidents is cited as a blemish on Congress ministries' record?
o: No political prisoners were ever released by any Congress ministry
The Bihar government reinstated the Rowlatt Act provisions
The Madras government arrested socialists Yusuf Maherally and S.S. Batliwala for inflammatory/seditious speeches
The Bombay government banned all trade unions outright

q: Which of the following constraints limited the Congress ministries from undertaking a complete overhaul of the agrarian structure, such as abolishing zamindari entirely?
o: Inadequate powers and financial resources, the need to conciliate landlord-dominated legislative councils, and the approach of the Second World War
A total lack of legislative majority in any province
British refusal to allow any land-related legislation whatsoever
Complete absence of any interest in agrarian reform

q: Regarding the benefits of the agrarian reforms undertaken by Congress ministries, which of the following is correct?
o: Most benefits went to statutory and occupancy tenants, while sub-tenants and unmobilised agricultural labourers gained little
No agrarian legislation was passed at all during this period
All classes of peasants, including agricultural labourers, benefited equally
Only zamindars benefited from the reforms

q: The Congress ministries' approach to labour issues was primarily aimed at:
o: Ignoring labour issues altogether
Advancing workers' interests while promoting industrial peace through compulsory arbitration and conciliation machinery
Fully nationalising all private industries immediately
Suppressing all trade union activity entirely

q: Which of the following was an example of extra-parliamentary mass activity undertaken by Congress during its rule in the provinces?
o: Direct armed confrontation with British forces
Formal alliance with the Muslim League government
Mass literacy campaigns, Congress police stations and panchayats, and Congress Grievance Committees
Complete withdrawal from all provincial governance

q: Which of the following is identified as a positive achievement of the 28-month period of Congress rule in the provinces?
o: It proved conclusively that dominion status was preferable to complete independence
It demonstrated that a movement could use state power to further its ends without being co-opted, and further weakened the myth that Indians were unfit to rule
It fully abolished the zamindari system nationwide
It eliminated all communal tensions in Indian society

q: The Congress ministries resigned from office in:
o: October 1939, following the outbreak of the Second World War
1937, immediately after being elected
1940, after the Lahore Resolution
1942, at the start of the Quit India Movement

q: Which of the following charges did the Pirpur Committee report level against Congress ministries?
o: Failure to implement any agrarian reforms whatsoever
Complete abolition of separate electorates for all minorities
Excessive support for Muslim League candidates in elections
Interference in religious rites, suppression of Urdu in favour of Hindi, and denial of proper representation to Muslims

q: Which of the following best summarises the overall significance of the 28-month period of Congress rule in the provinces, as assessed in the chapter?
o: It had no lasting political or administrative significance
It proved that colonial administration was entirely superior to any form of Indian self-rule

It confirmed that Indian self-government was necessary for social transformation, while also revealing the genuine difficulties of governing within a colonial constitutional framework amid high popular expectations
It resulted in the immediate abolition of British rule in India
